description: UXsim is a free, open-source macroscopic and mesoscopic network traffic flow simulator written in Python. It simulates the movements of car travellers and the formation of congestion on road networks and is intended for large, city-scale traffic phenomena, with a simple, lightweight and customisable design aimed at research and teaching. It is developed by Toru Seo with contributors on GitHub and distributed on PyPI (version 1.14.2 at the time of reading, with commits in August 2026), under the MIT licence and free of charge. The simulator is location independent: users define or import a network and demand for any city. Caveats: it models cars only in aggregate (no microscopic lane changing or public transport vehicles), so results suit network-level studies, not intersection design. It serves network flow and dynamic traffic assignment experiments, disruption and resilience tests (removing links and observing congestion), evacuation and emergency response scenarios and capacity planning; it is a lighter counterpart to SUMO and MATSim, both catalogued here.
